articles.headline: Anthropic rolls out Claude Opus 5: half‑price flagship with a 30.2 AGI score
articles.dek: Claude Opus 5 arrives at the same token price as its predecessor but delivers a 30.2 score on the AGI benchmark, new built‑in computer‑vision, and roughly 50 % lower cost than the Fable 5 baseline.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Claude Opus 5 is Anthropic’s newest flagship model that keeps Opus‑4’s token pricing while halving the effective cost and adding a 30.2 AGI‑benchmark score plus native vision capabilities — a change that directly lowers your inference bill and expands what you can build with a single API call. [FACT:318160249e1ef97aa4263ff1a3ae0d66][FACT:e32f0f393d7abbd190ad5339a543b8c9][FACT:a3cada91e91b2c43cfb2f65ff2c28a09][FACT:ecfddabc8b6ed7308ced991752910716][FACT:6691920baf40bbeb9c8e6a8b3c11f576]
Why This Matters

The model now leads the Artificial Analysis leaderboard, meaning it outperforms peers on logical reasoning and coding tasks, which translates into fewer retry calls for developers. Its half‑price token rate makes large‑scale batch jobs viable for startups and mid‑size teams. The built‑in vision layer removes the need for a separate image model, simplifying pipelines and cutting latency. However, Anthropic still warns that Claude should not be given password‑level access, so security hygiene remains essential. [FACT:338bf43573a1d8f0a6bc79c4f93acc0a][FACT:7f28e8135e1e538c2899ce3d9238ddf2][FACT:ae0d123495bb4c73ac6f88fcdcd96da4][FACT:abed9183a2d256b0c3e522e2d9342747][FACT:e2f1146ea3ad9d1b8647bae14a222dab]
What Happened

Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5 on July 24, 2026 as a direct upgrade to Opus 4. The token price stays unchanged, but the model’s internal efficiency gives an effective 50 % price cut compared to the previous Fable 5 benchmark. Benchmarks show a 30.2 score on the AGI “Arc” suite, the highest reported for any Anthropic model to date, and the model now responds to image inputs without a separate vision API. [FACT:318160249e1ef97aa4263ff1a3ae0d66][FACT:e32f0f393d7abbd190ad5339a543b8c9][FACT:a3cada91e91b2c43cfb2f65ff2c28a09][FACT:ecfddabc8b6ed7308ced991752910716][FACT:6691920baf40bbeb9c8e6a8b3c11f576]
Builder View

If you’re running inference on Opus 4 or Fable 5, switching to Opus 5 can shave up to half your token bill while giving you a stronger reasoning engine and instant vision support. That means fewer micro‑services, lower cloud spend, and faster time‑to‑value for mixed‑modal apps. Just remember to keep password handling out of Claude’s prompt surface, as Anthropic’s own security advisory still applies. [FACT:a3cada91e91b2c43cfb2f65ff2c28a09][FACT:0e48665c9fa6e6b46995f25e3c87ae68][FACT:e2f1146ea3ad9d1b8647bae14a222dab]
Open Questions

The announcement leaves a few gaps: exact latency numbers for the new vision path, roadmap for fine‑tuning Opus 5 on custom data, and when the model will be generally available outside the early‑access program. Builders will also want to track whether Anthropic tightens the password‑use policy in future releases. [FACT:70d31a4be8d82beb931a190907a78c80][confidence:low]
Ardur Take

Three independent sources confirm the claims, and the performance and cost metrics line up across Anthropic’s own blog and third‑party coverage, giving us high confidence that Opus 5 is both cheaper and more capable. For any team that’s already budgeting for LLM inference, the immediate ROI argument is strong enough to spin up a quick test bucket. [FACT:318160249e1ef97aa4263ff1a3ae0d66][FACT:e32f0f393d7abbd190ad5339a543b8c9][FACT:ae0d123495bb4c73ac6f88fcdcd96da4]

keyPoints: Claude Opus 5 keeps Opus‑4’s token price but halves effective cost versus Fable 5.
Achieves a 30.2 score on the AGI “Arc” benchmark, the highest for Anthropic models.
Adds native computer‑vision support, removing the need for a separate image model.
Leads the Artificial Analysis leaderboard, indicating stronger reasoning and coding ability.
